question.text: Which type of option typically has the HIGHEST gamma?

answer.text: Deep ITM options with long time to expiry
Deep OTM options with long time to expiry
ITM options at the start of the trading cycle

explanation.text: The Logic: Gamma measures the rate of change of delta with respect to the underlying. It is largest where delta changes most quickly per unit move in the underlying. That happens for ATM options near expiry: their outcome is most uncertain (could end ITM or OTM), so a small price change can swing delta dramatically (e.g., from around 0.5 toward 0 or 1) within a very short remaining life. The Trap: Deep ITM and deep OTM options already have deltas close to 1 or 0 respectively, so further price moves change delta only marginally — gamma is small. Long-dated ITM/ATM options have time on their side, so delta evolves more smoothly and gamma is lower than near expiry. Note: The cited NISM-Series-VIII workbook pages (77-78, 81, 124) define gamma and note that ATM options carry high uncertainty, but the specific ranking "gamma is highest for ATM options near expiry" was not located in the pages checked. The framing above is general options-Greeks theory rather than a direct workbook citation.
